name: Persona-specific operational-security rules govern speech, login surfaces, and response time zones

attribution.legal_posture: Defensive synthesis of cited public sources; the technique mapping supplies context rather than an identity attribution.

caveats: False-positive caution: Candidates may use assistive technology, interpreters, AI tools permitted by policy, or experience anxiety. Publish tool-use rules in advance and evaluate consistency and authorship rather than mannerisms.
Remote teams, shift work, travel, caregiving, and VPNs create time-zone variation; language fluency and filler words are contextual signals, with nationality and intent requiring corroboration.
The specific rules are a snapshot from one corpus and serve as examples rather than immutable signatures.

statements: BBC’s internal-rule evidence directs workers to rewrite technical answers into simple conversational English with natural fillers, avoid Gmail login on a shared PC so multiple identities are not exposed together, and answer clients on the claimed Serbian time zone. These are source-reported anti-correlation procedures, not immutable signatures.

sources.support: BBC reports explicit rules for conversational English, avoiding multi-identity Gmail exposure on shared PCs, and responding in the claimed time zone
The joint alert warns that no single behavior is definitive and indicators should be evaluated in combination
